correctness.rationale: For each unselected 2-subset uv, its number of selected disjoint 2-subsets is t-deg_H(u)-deg_H(v). This gives necessary-and-sufficient degree-sum bounds 2 at t=k+2 and 3 at t=k+3. The first excludes every smaller candidate; the second forces maximum degree at most 3, then either the complete K4 only when k=3 or exactly three degree-2 vertices forming a triangle with a disjoint k-edge matching. Both converses hold. Selected-edge neighborhoods separate the K4 exception from both tuple notions. Literal independent enumeration checks 2,351,118 candidate sets for k=2,3 at sizes k+2,k+3; the finite tests support but do not prove the general argument.

value.rationale: The exact boundary at which three domination numbers agree is mathematically motivated by published threshold theorems. The new infinite rigidity theorem answers whether that equality extends to the actual minimizing families: yes for all k>=2 except that k=3 admits precisely 126 extra labelled ordinary minima of a qualitatively different K4 type. The classification is complete and exposes a genuine difference between outside-only and closed/open neighborhood requirements. It is not merely the known matching count or a random small-case census.
